title: Extrapolation error, CQL, IQL, and a TD3+BC actor loss
brief: Watch Q-learning on a cautious demonstrator's data walk off the cliff, then fix the values with CQL or IQL, and penalize an actor that leaves the logged actions.
hints: action_counts(data, S, A) > 0 marks the pairs the data covers. In offline_q_iteration, update only those entries with np.where; the rest keep their starting 0.
To average targets per (s, a), np.add.at a table of sums at (data['s'], data['a']), then divide by the counts where they are positive.
The gradient of logsumexp over a row is its softmax. So cql_penalty_grad adds softmax(Q[s_i]) / N to row s_i and subtracts 1 / N at (s_i, a_i). Use np.add.at, because states repeat.
In cql_q_iteration, the TD part of the gradient is (Q[s, a] - y) / N added at (s, a). Divide row s of the total gradient by counts[s].sum() / N before the step.
The expectile loss weight is np.where(u < 0, 1 - tau, tau). Its gradient is 2 * weight * u / u.size; the weight is piecewise constant, so it has no derivative of its own.
iql_values never takes a max: V = expectile(Q, counts, tau), then the target is r + gamma * (1 - done) * V[s2].

bc_regularized_actor_loss sets lam = alpha / mean(abs(q_data)) and returns mean((pi_actions - data_actions)**2) - lam * mean(q_pi). Hold lam fixed. q_data is Q at the logged actions, not Q at the policy's actions.
